```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B has a named, sourced payer: the individual expat pays per filing season. Live competitor prices anchor willingness to pay ($119-$199 Expatfile, $175 MyExpatTaxes, $169 + $49 FBAR H&R Block, $199-$799+ Atamatax). A's own Payer section says 'No clean single payer found.'",
    "Every direct competitor in A is free to end users and funded by grants, VC or nonprofit dues. That is evidence against getting a paying customer within 90 days. B's competitors all charge, which shows the money exists.",
    "B's demand evidence is direct and tied to cost: a Reddit user quoted $800-$2,500 a year for a 'straightforward' situation, and others describe the forms as a 'nightmare.' A's demand quotes show people want the function, but none shows anyone paying for it.",
    "B cites a solo-founder precedent: Atamatax is described as 'built solo' and charging $199-$799+. This fits the one-person, AI-agent operating model. A's closest monetized analog, Pointz, needed $520k and years of work.",
    "B's main risk is scope: building the country-of-residence filing logic. That risk can be cut down by starting with a single country pairing or a US-side PFIC/FBAR wedge, and those still have a proven payer. A's main risk is that no payer exists at all, and narrowing scope does not fix that."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's 'Case For' claims a 'credible non-consumer payer path (municipal Vision Zero programs, research grants).' No source is given for any city or advocacy group paying a third party for this kind of tool. The brief's own Open Question #1 admits this is unknown, and the only funding evidence (BikeMaps.org's $930k government grant) went to a research institution, not to a solo vendor. Since this payer path is A's whole route to revenue, it effectively counts as missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-high confidence that B is the better first bet, but B has real uncertainties that could break the 90-day window. The IRS EFIN approval and software acceptance timeline is unquantified. The legality of self-serve country-specific tax advice is an open question. The combined US+local differentiator has no direct willingness-to-pay evidence. The claim that Atamatax 'attracts customers' rests on its pricing page, not on reported sales. A paying customer within 90 days is plausible for B only if the MVP is narrowed to a single wedge."
}
```
